topics.name: fever
patterns: I have chills and body heat
how to bring down a fever
topics.summary: A fever is usually the body's response to an infection and often settles within a few days.
self_care: Rest and drink plenty of fluids.
Wear light clothing and keep the room comfortably cool.
A fever reducer such as paracetamol can help; follow the label or ask a pharmacist for the right dose.
Check your temperature every few hours.
see_doctor: The fever lasts more than 3 days.
Temperature reaches 39.4 C (103 F) or higher.
A baby under 3 months has any fever.
There is a stiff neck, rash, confusion, severe headache or trouble breathing.

topics.name: headache
patterns: pain in my forehead and temples
how to get rid of a headache
topics.summary: Most headaches are tension headaches or migraines and ease with rest.
self_care: Rest in a quiet, dark room.
Drink water and do not skip meals.
Take a break from screens and ease neck and shoulder tension.
A simple pain reliever can help; follow the label or ask a pharmacist.
see_doctor: It is sudden and the worst headache of your life.
It comes with fever and a stiff neck.
It follows a head injury.
There is weakness, numbness, confusion, or a change in vision or speech.
Headaches keep coming back or keep getting worse.

topics.name: cold or cough
patterns: I think I caught the flu
how do I treat a common cold
topics.summary: Colds and most coughs are caused by viruses and usually clear on their own in one to two weeks.
self_care: Rest and drink plenty of warm fluids.
Breathe in steam or use a humidifier to ease congestion.
Saline nose drops or spray can help a blocked nose.
Honey in warm water can soothe a cough (not for children under 1 year).
see_doctor: Cold symptoms last more than 10 days, or a cough lasts more than 3 weeks.
You have trouble breathing or chest pain.
You have a high fever that does not settle.
You cough up blood.

topics.name: sore throat
patterns: my throat hurts when I swallow
how to soothe a sore throat
topics.summary: A sore throat is most often caused by a viral infection and usually improves within a week.
self_care: Gargle with warm salt water.
Drink warm fluids and stay hydrated.
Rest your voice.
Throat lozenges can help adults and older children.
see_doctor: It lasts more than a week.
You have difficulty swallowing, breathing or opening your mouth.
You have a high fever or swollen glands.
Sore throats keep coming back.

topics.name: diarrhoea
patterns: I think I have food poisoning
running to the toilet again and again
topics.summary: Diarrhoea is usually caused by an infection or something you ate and often settles in a day or two. The main risk is dehydration.
self_care: Drink plenty of fluids; oral rehydration solution (ORS) is best.
Eat small, bland meals such as rice, bananas, toast or curd.
Avoid oily, spicy and very sweet food until you recover.
Wash your hands often to avoid spreading it.
see_doctor: It lasts more than 2 days in an adult, or more than 24 hours in a child.
There is blood in the stool or the stool is black.
You have a high fever or severe stomach pain.
There are signs of dehydration: very little urine, dizziness, dry mouth.

topics.name: nausea or vomiting
topics.summary: Nausea and vomiting are often caused by a stomach infection or food and usually pass within a day or two.
self_care: Take small, frequent sips of water or ORS.
Avoid solid food until the vomiting stops, then start with bland food.
Rest, and avoid strong smells.
Avoid alcohol, caffeine and oily food.
see_doctor: You cannot keep fluids down for 24 hours.
There is blood in the vomit, or it looks like coffee grounds.
You have severe stomach pain or a severe headache.
There are signs of dehydration: very little urine, dizziness, dry mouth.

topics.name: constipation
patterns: I have not passed stool in three days
topics.summary: Constipation is common and usually improves with changes to diet and routine.
self_care: Eat more fibre: fruit, vegetables, whole grains and pulses.
Drink more water through the day.
Be physically active every day.
Do not ignore the urge to go, and give yourself time.
see_doctor: It lasts more than 2 to 3 weeks.
There is blood in the stool.
You have severe stomach pain or vomiting.
You are losing weight without trying.

topics.name: acidity or heartburn
patterns: burning feeling in my chest after eating
acid reflux and sour taste in mouth
too much gas in my stomach
topics.summary: Acidity and heartburn happen when stomach acid rises into the food pipe, often after large or spicy meals.
self_care: Eat smaller meals and eat slowly.
Do not lie down for 2 to 3 hours after eating.
Cut down on spicy, oily and acidic food, and on tea, coffee and alcohol.
Raise the head of your bed if symptoms come at night.
see_doctor: It happens more than twice a week or does not improve.
You have difficulty or pain when swallowing.
You are vomiting, or losing weight without trying.
Chest pain with sweating, breathlessness or pain spreading to the arm or jaw is an emergency.

topics.name: minor cut or wound
patterns: I got a graze from falling
how do I treat a minor wound
topics.summary: Most small cuts and grazes can be treated at home.
self_care: Wash your hands, then press on the cut with a clean cloth until bleeding stops.
Rinse the wound under clean running water.
Pat dry and cover with a clean dressing or plaster.
Change the dressing daily and keep the wound clean and dry.
see_doctor: Bleeding does not stop after 10 minutes of firm pressure.
The cut is deep, gaping, or has something stuck in it.
It was caused by an animal or human bite, or a dirty or rusty object.
It becomes red, swollen, warm, or has pus.
You are not sure your tetanus vaccination is up to date.

topics.name: minor burn
patterns: how to treat a small burn
topics.summary: Small, shallow burns can usually be treated at home.
self_care: Cool the burn under cool running water for 20 minutes.
Remove rings, watches and tight clothing near the burn before it swells.
Cover loosely with a clean, non-fluffy dressing or cling film.
Do not use ice, butter, oil or toothpaste, and do not burst blisters.
see_doctor: The burn is larger than the palm of your hand, or deep.
It is on the face, hands, feet, genitals or over a joint.
It was caused by chemicals or electricity.
It shows signs of infection: increasing pain, redness, swelling or pus.
The person is a young child or an older adult.

topics.name: sprain or strain
patterns: I twisted my ankle while running
my wrist is swollen after a fall
topics.summary: Mild sprains and strains usually improve over one to two weeks.
self_care: Rest the injured part and avoid activities that hurt.
Apply ice wrapped in a cloth for 15 to 20 minutes every few hours.
Use a compression bandage, not too tight.
Keep the injured part raised above heart level when you can.
see_doctor: You cannot put weight on it or move the joint.
There is severe swelling, bruising or the joint looks out of shape.
There is numbness or tingling.
It is not improving after a few days.

topics.name: back pain
patterns: pain in my back when I bend
topics.summary: Most back pain is caused by muscle strain and improves within a few weeks.
self_care: Stay as active as you can; long bed rest slows recovery.
Apply a heat pack to the sore area.
Avoid heavy lifting and check your sitting posture.
Gentle stretching can help once the pain eases.
see_doctor: You have numbness or weakness in the legs.
You lose control of your bladder or bowels; this is an emergency.
The pain started after a fall or injury.
You also have fever or unexplained weight loss.
It has not improved after a few weeks.

topics.name: mild allergy
patterns: my skin is itchy and red
I got a rash on my arm
itchy eyes and sneezing from dust
how to treat an itchy rash
topics.summary: Mild allergies cause sneezing, itchy eyes or an itchy rash and usually settle once you avoid the trigger.
self_care: Find and avoid the trigger if you can (dust, pollen, a food, a new product).
Wash the skin with cool water and avoid scratching.
A cool compress can ease itching.
Ask a pharmacist about an antihistamine that is suitable for you.
see_doctor: The rash spreads quickly, blisters, or does not improve in a few days.
You have fever with the rash.
Swelling of the lips, face or throat, or trouble breathing, is an emergency.

topics.name: dehydration
patterns: I feel very thirsty and dizzy
dry mouth and tired in the heat
how do I know if I am dehydrated
topics.summary: Dehydration happens when you lose more fluid than you take in. Signs are thirst, dark urine, a dry mouth, tiredness and dizziness.
self_care: Drink water in small, frequent sips.
Use oral rehydration solution (ORS) if you have had diarrhoea, vomiting or heavy sweating.
Rest in a cool place.
Avoid alcohol and too much caffeine.
see_doctor: You pass very little or no urine.
You feel confused, very drowsy or faint.
You cannot keep fluids down.
A baby or older person shows signs of dehydration.

topics.name: trouble sleeping
patterns: I wake up many times at night
I am not getting enough sleep
topics.summary: Trouble sleeping is common and often improves with a steady routine.
self_care: Go to bed and wake up at the same time every day.
Avoid caffeine in the evening and heavy meals late at night.
Put screens away for an hour before bed.
Keep the bedroom dark, quiet and cool.
Be active in the day, but not just before bed.
see_doctor: Poor sleep has lasted more than a month.
It affects your work, studies or mood.
You snore loudly and wake up gasping.

topics.name: stress or anxiety
patterns: I am anxious all the time
topics.summary: Stress and anxiety are common, and there are simple things that can help you feel steadier.
self_care: Try slow breathing: in for 4 counts, out for 6, for a few minutes.
Be physically active; even a short walk helps.
Keep regular sleep and meals.
Talk to someone you trust about what is on your mind.
Break big tasks into small steps.
see_doctor: It lasts more than 2 weeks or keeps getting worse.
It gets in the way of work, studies, sleep or relationships.
You have panic attacks.
You have thoughts of harming yourself; please seek help right away.

topics.name: blood pressure
patterns: what is a normal blood pressure
topics.summary: High blood pressure usually has no symptoms, so regular checks matter. A normal adult reading is below about 120/80 mmHg.
self_care: Cut down on salt and processed food.
Be active for about 30 minutes on most days.
Keep a healthy weight, and limit alcohol and tobacco.
Take prescribed medicines exactly as your doctor advised.
Check your blood pressure regularly and keep a record.
see_doctor: Your readings stay at or above 140/90.
You want to start, stop or change any medicine.
A very high reading with chest pain, severe headache, breathlessness or vision change is an emergency.

topics.name: diabetes
patterns: what are the signs of diabetes
topics.summary: Diabetes means blood sugar stays too high. Common signs are frequent urination, strong thirst, tiredness and slow-healing wounds.
self_care: Eat regular, balanced meals with fewer sugary foods and drinks.
Be physically active on most days.
Take medicines or insulin exactly as prescribed.
Check your blood sugar as your doctor advised.
Look after your feet and get regular eye checks.
see_doctor: You have signs of diabetes and have not been tested.
Your readings stay outside the range your doctor set.
You have a wound that is not healing.
Confusion, very fast breathing, or fainting needs urgent care.
